name: link_whoami
description: Which window of the desktop you are in, and which windows the person wired to yours (their number, the wire's name, the agent there and its folder).

name: link_list
description: The windows wired to yours: number, the wire's name, title, the agent that runs there (claude, codex…) and whether it works, is ready or waits for its person, and its folder.

name: link_delegate
description: Hand a task to the agent in a wired window (another Claude Code, Codex…), or —if you are a companion of a caravan— to any companion of yours by name, through its mailbox, with no wire. To a companion it is always asynchronous: end your turn after it; its answer comes to you as a new message. To a wired window: it is typed there as a pasted task saying it comes from you, and its answer comes back. With wait=false (the default) this returns at once and the answer —or a question it stops to ask on the way— is typed into your terminal when it is there; with wait=true this call returns the answer (or the question). This is how you talk to another agent the person wired to you: never start another agent of your own for it (codex exec, claude -p…), and never use the screen's cursor.

window.description: The window: its number from link_list, the name of its wire («tests»), or the agent that runs there («codex») if only one does.

task.description: What it has to do, as you would ask it.

wait.description: Wired windows only: wait here for its answer (true), or have it typed into your terminal later (false, the default). A companion is never waited for.

expects_reply.description: Companions: true, the default, for a request, a question or a task (its answer comes back to you). False for information that asks for no answer: a heads-up, a status, «done».

timeout.description: With wait=true, seconds to wait here (600). With wait=false its answer is brought however long it works; this many seconds without any sign of it working (6 hours if not said), and you are told it has not answered.

name: link_wait
description: Wait until the agent in a wired window is done with what it is doing, and get its answer; or what it stopped to ask its person.

window.description: The window: its number from link_list, the name of its wire («tests»), or the agent that runs there («codex») if only one does.

name: link_ask
description: What the agent in a wired window is asking its person now, if anything: a permission, a choice, a yes/no — the question and its options, the selected one marked.

window.description: The window: its number from link_list, the name of its wire («tests»), or the agent that runs there («codex») if only one does.

name: link_answer
description: Answer what the agent in a wired window asks: an option by its number or its words, free words where it lets you type them, or yes/no. The window shows who answered. The wire is the person's permission to do this.

window.description: The window: its number from link_list, the name of its wire («tests»), or the agent that runs there («codex») if only one does.

answer.description: An option's number ("2"), the words of an option, words to type, or yes/no.

name: link_read
description: The last lines of a wired window's terminal, as its screen and history show them.

window.description: The window: its number from link_list, the name of its wire («tests»), or the agent that runs there («codex») if only one does.

name: link_send
description: Type text into a wired window's terminal as a paste (and Enter after it, with enter=true). For a shell or a program there; to hand a task to an agent, link_delegate.

window.description: The window: its number from link_list, the name of its wire («tests»), or the agent that runs there («codex») if only one does.

name: link_keys
description: Press keys in a wired window's terminal, in order: enter tab escape up down left right backspace delete home end page_up page_down space ctrl+c, or one character. Returns its screen after.

window.description: The window: its number from link_list, the name of its wire («tests»), or the agent that runs there («codex») if only one does.

name: link_restart_me
description: Restart your own session, in this same conversation: what you added or changed since you started (an MCP server with `claude mcp add`, a skill, your settings) is only loaded by starting again. Only a companion (a named terminal) started by its shell can. After it, end your turn: a letter tells you to carry on, with `then` if you give it.

then.description: What to carry on with once you are back (your letter says it).

name: link_sent
description: Where the letters you sent to your companions are: waiting (and how many before), handed, being worked on, answered or not, each with how the one it went to is (free, working, in its shell, not started, could not start). Look here instead of asking a companion whether it got your letter: asking costs a turn of yours and of theirs. Only for a companion (a named terminal).

name: link_label
description: Give the wire to a window a name («tests», «frontend»): it is shown on the wire, and the window can be named by it.

window.description: The window: its number from link_list, the name of its wire («tests»), or the agent that runs there («codex») if only one does.

name: link_spawn
description: Open a new terminal with an agent (claude, codex…) beside your window, already wired to it, and hand it a task. Returns its window number; its answer comes as with link_delegate. If the agent asks something before it is ready (whether to trust the folder), the question is returned for you to answer with link_answer (whether to trust a folder is the person's call), and the task is handed by itself once it is.

model.description: The model it starts on, as that agent names it (claude-sonnet-5-5, gpt-6-luna…); its own default if not said.
